chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'but rather the ones from His servants who fear Allah are the scholars' [35:28]
He (peace be upon him) said: 'By "the scholars" it means those whose actions ratify their words; and whoever whose actions do not ratify his words, then he is not a scholar.'

key_terms.الْعُلَمَاءُ: scholars — here redefined by the Imam as those whose deeds confirm their words, not merely those with book knowledge
key_terms.صَدَّقَ فِعْلُهُ قَوْلَهُ: his actions ratify his words — the criterion for authentic scholarship
key_terms.يَخْشَى: fear (of Allah) — the reverent awe that comes from true knowledge of God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the meaning of 'scholars' in Quran 35:28?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a profound commentary on Quran 35:28, redefining 'scholar' not by intellectual attainment alone, but by the unity of word and deed. This teaching was directed at early Shia Muslims who needed guidance on the criteria for true religious authority, emphasizing that the feared-Allah scholars are those who embody their knowledge through action. The original audience would have understood this as a sharp distinction between authentic scholars whose conduct validates their speech and those who merely possess theoretical knowledge.

en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from al-Harith ibn Mughirah al-Nasri from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.)
